summary.text: Take \(n=8=2^3\), for which \(\Omega(8)=3\) is odd and at least three. Since \(\mu(4)=\mu(8)=0\), Möbius inversion gives \(a(8)=8!(H_8-H_4)=25584>0\), contradicting the predicted negative sign.

full_proof.text:
Let
\[
H_n=\sum_{j=1}^n \frac1j
\]
be the \(n\)-th harmonic number. The sequence \(a(n)\) is defined by
\[
\sum_{k\mid n}\frac{a(k)}{k!}=H_n.
\]
If we put \(b(k)=a(k)/k!\), this relation becomes
\[
\sum_{k\mid n}b(k)=H_n.
\]
Möbius inversion therefore gives
\[
b(n)=\sum_{d\mid n}\mu(n/d)H_d,
\]
and hence
\[
a(n)=n!\sum_{d\mid n}\mu(n/d)H_d,
\]
where \(\mu\) is the ordinary Möbius function.

We disprove the conjectured sign criterion by taking
\[
n=8.
\]
This is a positive integer, and its prime factorization is
\[
8=2^3.
\]
Consequently, the total number of prime factors counted with multiplicity is
\[
\Omega(8)=3.
\]
Thus \(\Omega(8)\) is odd and is at least \(3\). In other words, the right-hand side of the proposed equivalence
\[
a(n)<0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \bigl(\Omega(n)\text{ is odd and }\Omega(n)\ge 3\bigr)
\]
is true at \(n=8\).

It remains to determine the sign of \(a(8)\). The positive divisors of \(8\) are
\[
1,2,4,8.
\]
Therefore the Möbius-transform formula gives
\[
a(8)=8!\left(\mu(8)H_1+\mu(4)H_2+\mu(2)H_4+\mu(1)H_8\right).
\]
The integers \(8\) and \(4\) are both divisible by the square \(2^2\), so they are not squarefree. By the definition of the Möbius function,
\[
\mu(8)=0,\qquad \mu(4)=0.
\]
Also, \(2\) is prime, so
\[
\mu(2)=-1,
\]
and, as always,
\[
\mu(1)=1.
\]
Substitution reduces the expression to
\[
a(8)=8!\bigl(H_8-H_4\bigr).
\]
The difference of the harmonic numbers consists precisely of the terms from \(1/5\) through \(1/8\):
\[
H_8-H_4=\frac15+\frac16+\frac17+\frac18.
\]
Using the common denominator \(840\), this is
\[
\frac{168+140+120+105}{840}=\frac{533}{840}.
\]
Since \(8!=40320\) and \(40320/840=48\), we obtain
\[
a(8)=40320\cdot\frac{533}{840}=48\cdot533=25584.
\]
In particular,
\[
a(8)=25584>0,
\]
so the assertion \(a(8)<0\) is false.

Thus, for the positive integer \(8\), the condition on the number of prime factors is true—indeed, \(\Omega(8)=3\) is odd and at least \(3\)—while \(a(8)<0\) is false. Hence the two conditions are not equivalent for every positive integer. This counterexample disproves the conjecture.
